newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto conciliatory as parliament chooses speaker.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto conciliatory as parliament chooses speaker.

text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto sounded a conciliatory note on Sunday as she allowed her victorious opponents to choose a new National Assembly (lower house) speaker unopposed.
The 217-seat assembly, dominated by Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML), settled on PML nominee Ilahi Buksh Soomro, a veteran politician and former minister.
Departing speaker Yousaf Raza Gilani declared that Soomro had been chosen without a vote because the nominee of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), Khurshid Shah, had withdrawn.
Immediately after Soomro's election, Sharif walked over to Bhutto and both leaders smiled as they exchanged apparently friendly greetings, belying their bitter political rivalry.
Sharif publicly thanked Bhutto for withdrawing her party's nominations for speaker and deputy speaker.
"Such gestures should continue in the future too and I assure all the political parties in the house that I will uphold the democratic norms," he told the assembly.

Bhutto earlier confirmed that the 18 PPP members who survived the PML landslide in the February 3 general election would take up their seats in the National Assembly, retreating on a boycott threat made after the elections.

"We are not planning to boycott. We would like to see political stability and we would like to see the parliamentary forces strengthened," a subdued Bhutto told Reuters Television as she entered the parliament building in Islamabad.
"We hope this National Assembly will last longer than others," she said.
The PPP's nominee for deputy speaker, Naveed Qamar, who was appointed finance minister in the last days of Bhutto's rule, also said he hoped the assembly would serve its full term.
Qamar's withdrawal allowed Jaffar Iqbal of the PML to be chosen unopposed as Deputy Speaker.

President Farooq Leghari used controversial constitutional powers to dissolve the assembly on November 5 three years into its five-year term. At the same time, he sacked Bhutto, a former political ally, on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Bhutto's administration was the fourth elected government dismissed by a president in eight years.
Sharif, whose last government was terminated by presidential order in 1993, is due to be sworn in as prime minister on Monday to take over from caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.

Political commentators said Sharif had chosen Soomro for the post of speaker partly because of his reputation for honesty and partly to ensure that leaders from the populous province of Punjab do not dominate all the top jobs.
Sharif, Leghari and General Jehangir Karamat, chief of staff of the army, all hail from Punjab.
Soomro, a wealthy landowner from the southern province of Sindh and close to Sharif, has served in previous governments as education minister and minister of science and technology.
